title: In a Major Boost for the Right, Another Bolsonaro Nears Brazil’s Presidency
partialText: Flávio Bolsonaro’s first round lead leaves President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva three weeks to find the votes to stop Brazil’s, and Latin America’s, rightward shift.

title: Brazil Election Could Give Bolsonaro a Key Role in Trump’s Latin America Map
partialText: Flávio Bolsonaro, now the favorite to win Brazil’s presidency, would give President Trump a critical new ally in Latin America, particularly on security.

title: Trapped in a Kill Zone, a Ukrainian City Is Beginning to Starve
partialText: Evacuation is almost impossible and food is running out in Russian-occupied Oleshky, a city menaced by mines and drones.

title: Texas Pediatricians Face Paxton Investigations for Vaccinating Children
partialText: Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general and Republican Senate candidate, has alleged a sprawling profit-driven conspiracy. Pediatricians say the accusations are an attempt at intimidation.

title: They Argued About Trump at a Dog Park. Then They Pulled Their Guns.
partialText: What happened between two dog owners one April afternoon in Ohio will soon be scrutinized by a judge and jury as both men grapple with the consequences.

title: Alejandro G. Iñárritu Knows That ‘Digger’ Is Polarizing. That’s the Point.
partialText: Alejandro G. Iñárritu knows that “Digger” is polarizing. “I prefer that to the lukewarm reception,” he says of the climate-change satire with Tom Cruise.

title: ‘Digger’ Review: Even Tom Cruise Can’t Save This Strained Satire
partialText: Though mightily he does try. The star brings his usual high energy to the role of a Texas oil tycoon in Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s ponderous climate comedy.

title: High Interest Rates Aren’t Slowing the A.I. Boom. That’s a Problem for the Fed.
partialText: Rising borrowing costs are taking a toll on households and businesses. But they are doing little to dampen enthusiasm for investments in A.I. infrastructure, which are contributing to inflation.

title: The Campaign for Ohio’s Next Governor May Be the Ugliest in the Country
partialText: The candidates for Ohio governor have significant policy differences, but the campaign ads have been strikingly personal, with exaggerated portrayals of one candidate as a con artist and the other as a drunk.

title: Democrats Expect Record Number of Women in Party in House After Midterm Elections
partialText: Democrats are increasingly confident they will have a record number of women serving in the House next year, after backing women in competitive districts they are now positioned to win.

title: How Ketamine Emerged as a Key Factor in an Alleged Cornell Sex Assault
partialText: The powerful anesthetic has gained popularity as a party drug, including among a certain social set on the university’s campus.

title: As Students Protest Handling of Cornell Sexual Assault Case, a Building Is Vandalized
partialText: An administration building was defaced and a glass door smashed early Monday after an emotional week following revelations about 2024 sexual assault allegations.

title: A Supreme Court Battle Over Climate Change Begins
partialText: The justices are about to hear a lawsuit that could determine whether the oil industry faces billions of dollars in liability for damages caused by global warming.

title: Why Cities and States Are Fighting Climate Change in Courtrooms
partialText: Faced with a president who has called global warming a hoax, officials have filed dozens of suits against oil companies to try to cover the costs of extreme weather.

title: Congress Is Supposed to Be More Powerful Than the Supreme Court. Why Isn’t It?
partialText: Trump and his allies in the Capitol have revealed a problem that has been developing for decades.

title: Spain’s Leader Calls Early Election After Housing Crisis Roils Government
partialText: Pedro Sánchez, the Spanish prime minister, has faced challenges including a migration crisis and several corruption scandals involving his inner circle.

title: Burst of Attacks in Gulf Heightens Fears Over Fragile Energy Trade
partialText: Strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia came as the region’s exporters were getting more oil to the world market.

title: War With Iran Is Forcing the World to Reckon With Geography’s Power
partialText: Trade blockages in the Persian Gulf have reminded the world that there are forces as great as or greater than technology and globalization.

title: Why Saudi Arabia’s Last War in Yemen Turned Into a Quagmire
partialText: A Saudi-led coalition has announced a military campaign against the Iran-backed Houthi militia in the country, reviving memories of its previous effort.

title: Saudi and Yemeni Forces Attack Houthis to Retake Control of Red Sea Coast
partialText: The offensive is an effort to wrest control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait from the Houthis, a militia in Yemen backed by Iran.

title: How Congo’s Ebola Epidemic Got So Bad So Quickly
partialText: What happened in Mangala, where residents were left with little outside support, helps explain how this outbreak became the worst seen in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: This Is How AIPAC Lost Its Way
partialText: There remains an opportunity for the group to play a positive and honest role in American politics.

title: Brazil’s Problem Is Bigger Than Bolsonaro
partialText: Brazil is fertile ground for authoritarian politics, no matter who wins this election.

title: Dennis Hastert, Powerful Politician Disgraced by Child Sexual Abuse, Dies
partialText: The longest-serving Republican speaker of the House admitted in 2016 to abusing teenage boys decades earlier. He was 84.
